content:
Sam: Heads-up folks  I'm flying into Ottawa for a day trip and will be around ByWard Market. Looking for the best poutine and someplace with maple taffy (sugar shack vibes) nearby. Also any late-night ramen recs?

Evelyn: Welcome to town! For classic poutine you cant go wrong with 'La Banquise' vibes, but that's Montreal. In Ottawa, try 'BeaverTails' for maple treats and 'Smoke's Poutinerie' for solid poutine chains near the market.

Noah: If you're in ByWard Market, 'D'Arcy McGee' does pub poutine that's decent and the patio's nice. For maple taffy, there are seasonal sugar-shack pop-ups in winter close to the market, otherwise 'BeaverTails' (street stall) has maple pastries.

Rae: Late-night ramen: 'RIN' in the market area closes around 11pm most nights, good brothy bowls. If you need something open later, 'Menya' usually goes late on weekends.

Sam: Sweet. Any vegetarian poutine options? Teammate might join and prefers no meat.

Evelyn: Yes! 'Poutineville' lets you customize and has veg gravy + cheese curd substitutes. Also 'Mello's' near the east side does a vegan poutine with cashew-based cheese occasionally.

Noah: Also pro tip: the market has food trucks around lunch that do smaller, experimental poutines (good for trying different toppings). Check the north lot by the main fountain.

Rae: Quick pasteable list for maps:
```
Smoke's Poutinerie  ByWard Market, near 55 York St
D'Arcy McGee  44 York St, ByWard Market
BeaverTails stall  ByWard Market main promenade
Poutineville  75 William St
RIN Ramen  20 Clarence St
Menya Ramen  101 Bank St
```

Sam: Awesome, thanks. Anyone want to join for a quick poutine crawl Sat at 1pm? I'll be done with meetings by then. 37d

Evelyn: Maybe! Vote in poll.

lunchbot: Poll created "Ottawa poutine crawl Sat 1pm" Options: 1) Yes 2) No 3) Maybe. Vote with :one:/:two:/:three:.

Noah: Voted :one: 44d I'll bring cash for shares.

Rae: :three: (might be checking a later train).

Sam: Great, if poll says yes I'll lock a meeting spot by the fountain. Also any tips for quick maple taffy etiquette? First time 60a

Evelyn: Trick: pick the freshest taffy on the cone, don't double-dip, let it cool a sec before wrapping on the stick. If it's a pop-up, they usually hand you a napkin and a wooden stick.

Rae: And dress warm if it's outside 328 (if you're visiting in shoulder season).

Sam: Noted. Thanks everyone, will keep the thread posted after the crawl :)
